comment: Machine-readable Agent Matrix registry. THE source orchestrators consume programmatically (orchestrate.mjs validates plans against it; `orchestrate agents` prints it). Prose detail lives in the operator dashboard's onboarding contract (Aralia-operator-dashboard/docs/agent-matrix/sections/05-agent-offering-registration-contract.md) — when that changes, update this file. Statuses: ready | quota_limited | trial | benched | deprecated | unknown. A packet agent must have role 'worker', status ready/quota_limited, and dispatch wiring (dispatch.command, dispatch.type api with an endpoint, or dispatch.type agent-tool) to pass validatePlan. Every entry in `agents` carries a `vendor` string — the company that supplies the model or agent, or "unknown". It is descriptive metadata; validatePlan does not read it. Every entry also carries `matrixId` — the dashboard offering id in ../Aralia-operator-dashboard/.agent/orchestration/agent-offerings.json, or null for a local-only lane with no dashboard offering. `node tools/agora/orchestrate.mjs agents --matrix` diffs this file against the dashboard ledger through matrixId and prints every disagreement. A lane that must NOT follow the ledger carries `matrixOverride` with the reason; the diff accepts it and prints it. Do not hand-edit a lane without running the diff after.

codex-cli-resume.label: Codex CLI session resume
codex-cli-resume.notes: Only for sessions created by the Codex CLI version on PATH. The first desktop-session test failed because PATH resolved to 0.140.0 while the session belonged to 0.144.0-alpha.4. Use codex-session-turn-once for version-matched desktop and CLI sessions. Session ids belong in .agent/agora/watchdog-targets.json, never in this tracked registry.

codex-session-turn-once.label: Codex version-matched one-shot heartbeat turn
codex-session-turn-once.notes: The watcher reads the saved session's cli_version, finds the matching locally installed Codex engine, resumes that session for one Agora heartbeat turn, then opens the same technical thread through the documented codex://threads/<thread-id> desktop route. No desktop message injection or keyboard automation is required.

codex-app-heartbeat.label: Codex app recurring in-thread heartbeat
codex-app-heartbeat.notes: Not used for Agora wake delivery. Its recurring minimum cadence adds polling delay; the event-driven codex-session-turn-once adapter is preferred.

claude-desktop-native.label: Claude Desktop native conversation watcher
claude-desktop-native.notes: Identity-safe placeholder for the intended Claude Desktop conversation. It must not fall through to claude-cli-resume, which is a different harness. Test 1 proved Vega's in-session native watcher; a supported external Desktop wake bridge is still missing.

claude-cli-resume.label: Claude CLI session resume
claude-cli-resume.notes: Resumes one known Claude Code session through the installed CLI. Native Claude Desktop message injection remains unclaimed.

claude.label: Claude subagent (Agent tool)

matrixOverride.reason: The dashboard benches the `claude` CLI surface for Matrix worker dispatch. This row is a different surface: the in-process Agent-tool subagent lane. tools/agora/ORCHESTRATOR.md keeps it as the default worker, so it stays ready. Bench the CLI surface, not this lane.

claude.notes: Default worker. Dispatched by the orchestrator via the Agent tool with the prompt from `orchestrate prompt <plan> <packet>`; a script cannot spawn Claude subagents.

codex.label: Codex CLI (gpt-5.5)

constraints.note: usage quota resets ~2am — probe before dispatch
benched for worker dispatch by operator policy; reserved for the orchestrator/supervisor role

codex.notes: Proven orchestrator workhorse. The dashboard benches it for worker dispatch, and this row matches that. Orchestrator use is unchanged. Honors .gitignore — inline full specs in the prompt, never point it at .agent/scratch paths.

codex-spark.label: Codex CLI — GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark (fast worker lane)

constraints.note: Has its OWN usage quota, SEPARATE from the `codex` orchestrator lane — Spark packets do not eat the orchestrator's budget, so this lane can run in parallel with `codex` without contention. Probe before dispatch

text-only, 128k context. Strong on targeted edits and rapid frontend/iteration loops; weak on multi-step architecture and stateful debugging (SWE-Bench Pro ~56% vs ~72% for full Codex 5.3) — do NOT give it deep refactors or cross-cutting design work

codex-spark.notes: Real-time coding model, Cerebras-served at 1000+ tok/s (~15x standard Codex). Research preview. Verified reachable on this account 2026-07-14: `codex exec -m gpt-5.3-codex-spark ...` returned PROBE_OK. No dashboard offering covers this model lane, so matrixId is null. Use for fast, well-scoped packets. Honors .gitignore like the codex lane — inline full specs in the prompt, never point it at .agent/scratch paths.

gemini.notes: Deprecated for new coding-worker lanes (2026-06); the dashboard benches it too. Historical sessions are preserved for audit only.
